<reason>A wins the cost-versus-exclusion comparison. It offers plausible phased fleet and dispatch mechanisms, answers the rationing question directly, and explains why absolute service floors can preserve substantial inequality. B identifies genuine proximity constraints and risks to thinly served areas, but repeatedly moves from necessary investment to ruinous oversupply without establishing that stronger conclusion. A does not prove affordability everywhere, but provides the more convincing justification for making comparable access an enforceable obligation.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A distinguishes sufficient accessible coverage from exclusively idle capacity and explicitly accepts modest edge-frequency reductions if necessary. B correctly challenges whether those reductions would remain modest, but its answer to why compliance must be ruinous largely restates that additional capacity costs money rather than resolving the comparative burden.</best_rebuttal>
